features.name: any_counter_rhetorical_question
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment by another user contain a rhetorical question?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one comment contains a rhetorical question asked by the commenter in their own voice: a question posed for rhetorical effect or to make a point, not to genuinely seek information or clarification from the OP. Genuine information-seeking questions, and questions only appearing inside quotations of others (unless the commenter adopts them), do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, outcome reports or post-outcome updates as evidence. Return 0 for a valid empty list; null if missing or malformed.

h0: any_counter_rhetorical_question has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Rows with any_counter_rhetorical_question = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than rows with 0.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Operationalized as presence of at least one rhetorical question in any counter-comment (the hypothesis does not specify count or share). Rhetorical vs genuine question is a judgment. OC_comments are unordered, with no timestamps; comments may contain outcome-related text, which is excluded from the semantic judgment. Association only, not causal.
